title: Even the holy still stumble from weakness
source_text: XXIV. Neque vero sanctitas & justitia fidelium simpliciter a summo perfectionis gradu in hac vita deficit, sed multis quoque naevis est obscurata; nec obstat quominus qui ea praediti sunt in peccata saepius ex infirmitate labantur. Hae sunt enim ipso-rum Apostolorum voces; In multis offendimus omnes. Jac. 3. 2. Item, Si dixeri-mus nos peccatum non habere, ipsi nos seducimus, & veritas in nobis non est. 1 Joh. 1. 8. Ac propterea Salomon universe pronunciat, Non est homo justus in terra, qui faciat bonum, & non peccet. Eccl. 7. 20. id est, sic justus ut semper bonum faciat, absque ullo peccato.
pass_a_gloss: Nor does the holiness and righteousness of believers simply fall short of the highest degree of perfection in this life, but it is also obscured by many blemishes; nor does it prevent those endowed with it from often falling into sins from weakness. For these are the very voices of the apostles: In many things we all offend (James 3:2). Likewise, If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us (1 John 1:8). And therefore Solomon universally pronounces: There is not a just man on earth who does good and does not sin (Ecclesiastes 7:20)—that is, so just as always to do good without any sin.
pass_b_english: Holiness is also spotted by many blemishes; the holy still fall from weakness.
Jas 3:2; 1 Jn 1:8; Eccl 7:20: no one on earth always does good without sinning.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1058.
